newsitem.title: USA: Ford sees improved July U.S. vehicle sales.
newsitem.headline: Ford sees improved July U.S. vehicle sales.

text.p: Ford Motor C. Automotive Operations President Jacques Nasser said the company's U.S. July vehicle sales will be stronger than the June level.
"It looks pretty good," Nasser told reporters at a news conference here when asked about Ford's sales for the month.
"June was a little weaker than what we had anticipated," Nasser added. "We think July has been stronger."
Ford's June U.S. car and light truck sales totaled 357,741 units, up 4.7 percent from the June 1996 level.

Nasser said Ford sees no major changes in the U.S. passenger car market in the second half of 1997 compared with the first half. Nasser said Ford is "quite pleased" with the incentives and other marketing programs that it has in the marketplace.

Nasser appeared at the Concours d'Elegance classic car show at Meadow Brook Hall here to unveil a new Mercury Division concept car called the MC2. Nasser said the concept will be the basis for an all-new Mercury Cougar specialty sports coupe that will be introduced as a 1999 model.

Lincoln-Mercury General manager James O'Connor said the automaker expects to sell more than 50,000 of the new Cougars in the United States annually. Ford also plans to introduce the car under the Cougar name in Europe at about the same time the U.S. version debuts. Ford officials would not say where the new Cougar would be built, although they said both Europe and the U.S. would be served by the same plant.

Industry analysts have said they expect the new Cougar will go into production in the summer of 1998 at Ford's AutoAlliance joint venture with Mazda Motor Corp in Flat Rock, Mich. The plant builds Mazda's 626 and MX6 cars and recently ended production of the Ford Probe sport coupe.
